desc: A scholar who reads fate in the stars. Heir to the school of glintstone sorcery.
whatItIs: A thin, bookish scholar who opens with a glintstone sorcery spellbook and a Dexterity score high enough to swing a light blade. The stat spread leans hard into Intelligence, so casting is the clear path from the first grace point.
whyItMatters: It suits a first-time run that wants to stand at range and zap enemies without trading blows. The low Vigor and Endurance make every hit felt, and the thin physical profile gives little forgiveness against a strong swing.
whenToUse: Pick it when a pure Intelligence casting build is the goal, especially glintstone sorcery with a touch of Dexterity for a secondary weapon. Skip it if melee is the priority, because the stat spread makes a Strength or Faith build costly to chase later.
name: Astrologer

desc: A dangerous bandit who strikes for weak points. Excels at ranged combat with bows.
whatItIs: A rough-fisted bowman who opens with a solid Arcane score and a Dexterity high enough to draw fast and stay mobile. The kit points toward keeping enemies at range and hitting weak points from cover.
whyItMatters: It suits a run that wants to snipe weak points and apply status effects from a distance. The Vigor and Endurance are modest, so a direct melee exchange is still dangerous, and the low Faith leaves healing incantations thin.
whenToUse: Choose it when a Dexterity or Arcane bow build is the plan from the opening hours. Avoid it if a heavy two-handed weapon is the goal, since the stat spread leaves little room for that path without extensive leveling.
name: Bandit

desc: A church spy adept at covert operations. Equally adept with a sword as they are with their incantations.
whatItIs: Part sword, part prayer. The character opens with high Faith and enough Strength to swing a decent blade, and the kit points toward trading blows while topping up with a healing incantation.
whyItMatters: It suits a build that wants to mix melee and Faith-based spells in one run. The Mind is solid for slotting a few incantations, but the low Intelligence means a sorcery-focused path would be a poor fit.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Faith-and-steel hybrid is the goal, especially if healing incantations and a sword feel natural. Skip it for a pure caster or a pure Strength tank, because the split stats leave both sides a little short.
name: Confessor

desc: A stalwart hero, at home with a battleaxe, descended from a badlands chieftain.
whatItIs: A broad-shouldered axe fighter who opens with a battle axe and a stat spread that favors heavy, close-range combat. Strength and Vigor are both high, and the kit points toward swinging a large blade with full commitment.
whyItMatters: A new character who wants to feel durable and land big two-handed swings finds a natural home here. The low Intelligence and Faith make casting a distant thought, while the modest Dexterity keeps a one-handed blade within reach if the axe feels clumsy.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Strength build is the plan and a heavy weapon is the comfort zone. Skip it for a caster or a fast Dexterity fighter, because the stat spread puts those builds at a noticeable disadvantage.
name: Hero

desc: A prisoner bound in an iron mask. Studied in glintstone sorcery, having lived among the elite prior to sentencing.
whatItIs: Bound in an iron mask, the character opens with Dexterity and Intelligence sitting close together, which keeps both a blade and a sorcery staff viable from the start. The kit points toward a hybrid that alternates between sword work and glintstone spells.
whyItMatters: It suits a build that wants to alternate between melee combos and ranged spells, or a caster who still wants a reliable sword option. The low Faith is the main gap, so any Faith-dependent build would be a stretch.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Dexterity-and-Intelligence hybrid is the goal, especially a sword-and-sorcery style. Skip it if Faith or pure Strength is the plan, since the stat spread does not fuel those paths well.
name: Prisoner

desc: A seer ostracized for inauspicious prophecies. Well-versed in healing incantations.
whatItIs: Ostracized for inauspicious prophecies, the character opens with high Faith and a Mind high enough to hold a solid spell repertoire. The kit leans toward healing incantations and defensive magic rather than raw damage.
whyItMatters: It suits a support-style build that wants to keep HP topped up and apply buffs while a spear and shield cover the melee side. The Endurance is thin, so long fights drain the stamina bar quickly, and the low Dexterity makes fast weapons feel sluggish.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Faith build is the plan and healing or buff incantations are the priority. Skip it for a Dexterity or Intelligence build, because the stat spread puts those paths at a clear disadvantage.
name: Prophet

desc: A capable fighter from the distant Land of Reeds. Handy with katana and longbows.
whatItIs: Handy with a katana and a longbow from the first grace point, the character opens with a Dexterity score that makes fast, mobile combat feel natural. The kit points toward quick katana work with a longbow as a backup.
whyItMatters: It suits a build that wants fast, agile melee with the option to step back and shoot. The low Faith and Arcane keep casting and status-effect builds out of reach early, and the Intelligence is too low for a sorcery path.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Dexterity katana build is the plan, especially one that leans into bleed, though the stats support a Strength-leaning katana build too. Skip it only for a pure caster, since the low Faith, Intelligence, and Arcane leave spellcasting out of easy reach.
name: Samurai

desc: A knight exiled from their homeland to wander. A solid, armor-clad origin.
whatItIs: Armor-clad and sturdy, the character opens with high Strength and Vigor and a kit that points toward slow, deliberate, heavy-hitting combat. The Dexterity is high enough for a one-handed blade, but the real strength is in durability.
whyItMatters: A beginner looking to feel sturdy and trade blows without panic finds a comfortable starting point here. Casting is a distant side thought given the low Intelligence and Faith, and the Dexterity supports a sword but not fast, agile play.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Strength melee build is the goal and survivability matters more than speed. Skip it for a caster or a glass-cannon Dexterity build, because the stat spread is the opposite of what those need.
name: Vagabond

desc: A nomad warrior who fights wielding two blades at once. An origin of exceptional technique.
whatItIs: Dual blades in hand and a high Dexterity score define the opening kit, making fast two-sword combat feel natural from the start. The stat spread points toward aggressive, mobile sword work in both arms.
whyItMatters: It suits a build that wants to juggle two weapons and keep the attack rate high. The low Faith and Arcane limit any hybrid plans, and the Strength is just enough for a one-handed blade but not a two-hander.
whenToUse: Pick it when a Dexterity dual-wield build is the plan from the start, though the starting stats leave room to lean into Strength as a second stat too. A caster is the one build to steer away from here, since Faith, Intelligence, and Arcane all start on the low side.
name: Warrior

desc: A poor, purposeless sod, naked as the day they were born. A nice club is all they have.
whatItIs: The barest of starts: a wooden club, no armor, and every stat set to the same modest number. Nothing is pre-baked, so the build is entirely up to the choices made in the first few hours.
whyItMatters: It suits a run that wants total freedom and does not mind a rough early game. The lack of starting gear means the first few enemies hit harder, and there is no class identity to fall back on if the chosen build does not click.
whenToUse: Pick it when a specific build is already planned and the starting stats do not matter. Skip it for a first-time run that wants a handrail, because the bare start offers no guidance on which path to take.
name: Wretch
